title: Spotting the Scam
introduction: In this module, you will learn how to recognise common scam warning signs and how to check suspicious messages safely.

sections.heading: What is a financial scam?
paragraphs: A financial scam is when someone tries to trick you into giving them money or personal information, such as your bank details, passwords or security codes. Scammers may contact you by phone, text message, email or social media, or through fake websites. Scams can be very convincing, and anyone can be targeted.
tips: Your bank will never ask you to share your full password, your PIN or a security code sent to your phone.

sections.heading: Common warning signs
paragraphs: Scam messages often share the same warning signs. Be careful if someone asks for money or personal details when you were not expecting it, offers something that sounds too good to be true, or asks you to keep it secret. Not every unexpected message is a scam, but these signs are a good reason to slow down.
tips: Be wary of anyone who pressures you to act straight away. A genuine organisation will give you time to check.

sections.heading: People pretending to be trusted organisations
paragraphs: Scammers often pretend to be from an organisation you trust, such as your bank, a delivery company or a government department. A familiar name or phone number can easily be copied. For example, a text might say your parcel could not be delivered and ask you to pay a small fee through a link to a fake website.
tips: Do not use a phone number or link given in a suspicious message. Find the official contact details yourself instead.

sections.heading: How to check a suspicious message
paragraphs: If something does not feel right, take a moment before you reply, click or pay. Do not open links or attachments you are unsure about. Instead, contact the organisation using its official website, its app or a phone number you already trust, such as the one on the back of your bank card.
tips: If you are still unsure, ask a family member or friend for help. Asking for help is a sensible step, not something to feel embarrassed about.

quiz.question: A text message says your parcel could not be delivered and asks you to pay a small fee using a link. What is the safest thing to do?
options: Pay the fee quickly so the parcel is not sent back.
Reply to the message and ask whether it is real.
Do not use the link, and check with the delivery company through its official website or app.
quiz.explanation: Links in unexpected messages can lead to fake websites. Checking through the delivery company's official website or app lets you find out whether the message is genuine.

quiz.question: Which of these is a common warning sign of a scam?
options: Being told you must act immediately and keep it a secret.
Receiving a letter you were expecting from your bank.
Finding contact details on an organisation's official website.
quiz.explanation: Scammers often create pressure and ask for secrecy so you do not have time to check or talk to anyone. A genuine organisation will give you time to make sure.
